description:
“Trump showed real sympathy for Beijing’s stance on Taiwan.”

Xi Jinping is trying to lock Trump into a more predictable US-China relationship, while subtly pushing America toward a softer stance on Taiwan, says chief China correspondent for the Wall Street Journal Lingling Wei.

Lingling Wei was speaking to Ryan Tubridy on Times Radio. Listen live every Sunday from 1-4pm.

“Andy Burnham did not grasp the nettle in relation to the final part of that review.”

Andy Burnham initially showed courage by reopening scrutiny into grooming gang inquiries in Greater Manchester, but ultimately failed to confront ongoing problems inside the system, says former police detective for the Greater Manchester Police Maggie Oliver.

Maggie Oliver was speaking to Adam Boulton with Sunday Mornings on Times Radio. Listen live every Sunday from 10am-1pm.

author: Times News
description:
Britain’s ultra-wealthy are on the move. One in six names from the 2024 Rich List have vanished, billionaires are decamping to Monaco and Switzerland, and a new generation of “laptop entrepreneurs” is overtaking the old landed fortunes. Robert Watts unpacks the five trends shaping The Sunday Times Rich List 2026 — from the Beckhams’ billion-pound empire to the post-Soviet titans now dominating the top 10.

author: Times News
description:
“Streeting knew exactly what he was doing. This is a Brexit-supporting old, disaffected, working-class, labour constituency that is ripe to be taken by Reform.”

Ex-health secretary Wes Streeting is playing a “game of politics” in announcing his desire to rejoin the EU, putting his leadership rival Andy Burnham's campaign in an awkward position for the Brexit-backing constituency of Makerfield, says The Sunday Times commentator Jason Cowley.

Jason Cowley was speaking to Rosie Wright and Calum Macdonald on Times Radio Breakfast. Listen live every day from 6-10am.
